_meta.indication: Adjunct to a low-fat diet and other lipid-lowering treatments, including LDL apheresis where available, to reduce LDL-C, total cholesterol, apolipoprotein B, and non-HDL-C in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH)

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multinational, open-label, single-arm trial; each subject served as his or her own control; lomitapide as add-on at individually defined maximum tolerated dose between 5 and 60 mg once daily for 78 weeks (weeks 0-26 efficacy phase, weeks 26-78 safety)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH) on stable diet and maximally tolerated LDL-lowering drugs, with or without apheresis
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent change from baseline to Week 26/end of treatment in directly measured serum LDL-C
pivotal_trials.result: Mean relative change in LDL-C from baseline to Week 26 was -40% (95% CI -52 to -27; p<0.001); 19 of 29 patients (66%) had LDL-C reductions ≥25%, with 8 (28%) achieving LDL-C <100 mg/dL

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥28%) are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, dyspepsia, and abdominal pain; gastrointestinal reactions occurred in 27 (93%) of 29 patients (diarrhea 79%, nausea 65%, dyspepsia 38%, vomiting 34%). Hepatotoxicity: 10 (34%) of 29 patients had at least one ALT/AST ≥3x ULN and 4 (14%) ≥5x ULN; median absolute increase in hepatic fat was 6%
target_moa: First-in-class small molecule inhibitor of microsomal triglyceride transfer protein (MTP), which transfers lipids to apolipoprotein B; MTP inhibition prevents assembly and secretion of apo B-containing lipoproteins (including VLDL-C, the precursor of LDL-C) and chylomicrons from liver and intestine

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF HEPATOTOXICITY — JUXTAPID can cause elevations in transaminases; 10 (34%) of 29 patients had at least one ALT or AST ≥3x ULN; it also increases hepatic fat; available only through a restricted REMS program

rems.type: JUXTAPID is available only through a restricted program called the JUXTAPID REMS PROGRAM, with elements to assure safe use (ETASU) to educate prescribers about hepatotoxicity risk and limit access to patients with a clinical phenotype consistent with HoFH

advisory_committee.vote: Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC), 17 October 2012: 13 members voted in favor, 2 against marketing of lomitapide for HoFH

summary.text: Lomitapide (Juxtapid), a first-in-class small-molecule MTP inhibitor, received orphan drug designation for HoFH (23 Oct 2007) and was approved as a traditional approval based on the surrogate endpoint of serum LDL-C in a single Phase 3 single-arm open-label trial of 29 HoFH patients, supported by a 13-to-2 EMDAC vote and requiring a REMS for hepatotoxicity risk

requirement.text: 1974-1: A juvenile animal toxicology study to evaluate the effects of lomitapide on neurological development, growth, and long bone development with and without vitamin and essential fatty acid supplementation

citations.quote: **1974-1:** A juvenile animal toxicology study to evaluate the effects of lomitapide on neurological development (learning, memory, behavior, and coordination), growth, and long bone development with and without vitamin and essential fatty acid supplementation to determine whether any observed effects are due directly to lomitapide or secondarily to the inhibition of absorption of fat soluble vitamins and/or essential fatty acids. This study should be completed before any formal pediatric studies are initiated.

citations.quote: **1974-2:** An assessment and analysis of spontaneous reports of malignancy, teratogenicity, and hepatic abnormalities in patients treated with Juxtapid (lomitapide) for a period of 10 years from the date of approval. Specialized follow-up should be obtained on these cases to collect additional information on the reports.

requirement.text: 1974-3: A long-term prospective observational study (product exposure registry) of HoFH patients treated with Juxtapid to evaluate known and potential serious risks including hepatic transaminase elevations, hepatic steatosis, small bowel and hepatic malignancies, teratogenicity, death, and major adverse cardiovascular events

citations.quote: **1974-3:** A long-term prospective observational study (product exposure registry) of patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH) treated with Juxtapid (Iomitapide) to evaluate known and potential serious risks related to the use of Juxtapid (Iomitapide), including hepatic transaminase elevations, hepatic steatosis, small bowel and hepatic malignancies, teratogenicity, death (including cause of death), and major adverse cardiovascular events (including cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, unstable angina, and revascularization procedures). The registry will continue for 10 years from the date of last patient enrollment.
